hook.evidence: Highlights growth of UAV swarms and need for intelligent networking/collaboration with CI.

gap.evidence: Notes prior surveys treat networking or collaboration separately and lack CI-based joint treatment.

yes_but.evidence: Acknowledges existing UAV networking and collaboration surveys but stresses missing unified CI focus.

contribution.evidence: Lists contributions: dual coverage of networking and collaboration, CI taxonomy, mission-specific surveys, future trends.

organization.evidence: Provides roadmap for sections II-X and references structure figure.

scope_boundary.evidence: Scope limited to CI-based networking and collaboration missions (channel access, routing, task assignment, path planning, search, jamming).

rhetorical_moves_global.reader_contract_pattern: Motivate UAV swarm needs; note lack of CI-based joint survey; outline CI taxonomy and mission-specific coverage; conclude with challenges and future directions.

taxonomy.classification_strategy: by mission and CI method family
axes: Mission (networking, collaboration, task assignment, path planning, search, jamming)
CI method family (heuristic behavior search, policy design, policy learning, hybrid)

visuals_tables.layout_logic: Intro uses figures for applications and structure; related work uses a comparison table; each mission section includes occasional figures for scenarios or taxonomies; lessons are text-heavy.

figures.purpose: show UAV swarm application scenarios motivating the survey
depict organizational structure and mission taxonomy

tables.purpose: contrast related surveys and coverage of missions

lesson_blocks.lesson: DRL and hybrid methods improve adaptability for channel access and routing in dynamic UANETs.
Four-family CI framing reveals trade-offs between optimality and adaptability across missions.
Hybrid and learning-based planners address dynamic environments better than pure heuristics.
Side-information and hybrid CI approaches enhance robustness in uncertain search/jamming contexts.
Future work should target scalability, security, and digital twins to accelerate CI learning for swarms.

synthesis.aha_moment: Using a repeated four-family CI taxonomy across all missions makes a large UAV-swarm design space comparable and shows where adaptability vs optimality trade-offs recur.

methodology.selection_criteria: keywords and databases listed (IEEE, ACM, AIAA, Elsevier, Springer, Taylor & Francis, Scientific, SIAM, Wiley, Hindawi)

style.section_openers_pattern: Introduce mission context then enumerate CI families with parallel subheadings and figures/tables as anchors.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Gap framing with dual-domain contrast
steps: Motivate mission needs and note split between networking-only and collaboration-only surveys.
Use a comparison table to show coverage gaps.
Follow immediately with contribution bullets and organization map.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Makes the missing joint treatment tangible and sets reader expectations early.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Reusable four-family CI taxonomy
steps: Define four CI families (heuristic search, policy design, policy learning, hybrid).
Apply the same four subheadings in every mission section for parallelism.
Close each mission with a short lessons-learned subsection.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Parallel structure lets readers compare missions quickly and spot pattern reuse.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Mission-by-mission deep dives after framework
steps: After introducing the global CI families, dedicate separate sections to each mission (task assignment, path planning, search, jamming).
For each mission, start with problem framing, then walk through the four families.
Summarize mission-specific lessons before moving on.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Keeps global taxonomy consistent while accommodating mission-specific nuances.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Challenges tied back to mission gaps
steps: Aggregate challenges observed across networking and mission sections.
Map future directions to the recurring trade-offs (scalability, security, adaptability).
Reinforce these directions briefly in the conclusion.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Shows a direct line from survey findings to a research agenda and closes the loop.
